m:alcazaba: Open every day: from 1 April to 31 October 9am–8pm (last entry 7pm), from 1 November to 31 March 9am–6pm (last entry 5pm) (City Council website, alcazabaygibralfaro.malaga.eu). Ticket €7 for one monument, €10 with Gibralfaro Castle (reduced €3 and €5). One guide says entry is free on Sundays from 2pm: I didn't find this on the official website, to be confirmed. On Mondays the lift to the Nasrid palaces may be out of service (guide, to be confirmed).
m:gibralfaro: Same hours as the Alcazaba: 9am–8pm until 31 October, 9am–6pm from 1 November (last entry an hour before). Gibralfaro only €7, combined ticket with the Alcazaba €10 (City Council website). EMT bus line 35 goes up from the centre to the castle (to be confirmed on emtmalaga.es). The walk up is steep: comfortable shoes and water.
m:teatro: Entry is free (guide, to be confirmed). I couldn't find the official hours: check malaga.eu before going. You can also see it well from outside, from the street.
m:catedral: Open Monday–Friday 10am–6:30pm (in summer until 8pm; the website gives hours that don't match: to be confirmed), Saturday 10am–6pm, Sunday and holidays 2–6pm; last entry 45 minutes before closing. Ticket €10 with audio guide (official website malagacatedral.com); one guide gives €12 with the rooftops. The rooftop climb is separate, by booking. Closed on 25 December and 1 January; on 24 and 31 December 10am–3pm. Dress modestly. On Saturdays and Sundays it can't be visited during services.
m:picasso: Open every day 10am–7pm (from a guide, to be confirmed on the museum's website: in some periods it opens later). The collection costs €9.50 (reduced €7.50); with temporary exhibitions up to €12. Free entry on Sundays in the last two hours and on some days of the year, including 27 October, the museum's anniversary (guide, to be confirmed).
m:pompidou: Open every day except Tuesday, 9:30am–8pm (last entry 30 minutes before), holidays included; on 24 and 31 December it closes at 3pm (from a listing, to be confirmed on the museum's website). Tickets from €9 (permanent collection plus temporary exhibitions; Ticketlens). Free entry on Sundays from 4pm (guide, to be confirmed).
m:thyssen: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–8pm (last entry 30 minutes before), closed on Mondays except 18 May, 12 October and 7 December. On 24 and 31 December it closes at 3pm; closed on 25 December, 1 and 6 January. Ticket €12 (€15 with the archaeological site), reduced €8 (official website, fares from January 2026). Free on Sundays from 4pm.
m:atarazanas: Open Monday to Saturday 8am–3pm, closed on Sundays (guides; to be confirmed). For the fish it's best to go before 11am. Entry is free. To eat, the stalls near the entrance cost more; the bar inside makes pescaíto and boquerones.
m:larios: Free to walk at any hour. Shops usually open 10am–9pm and many stay open on Sundays in the centre too. The Christmas lights are switched on from late November (date to be confirmed).
m:muelle: Free to walk around. Shops and venues have their own hours: they generally open from 10am and close late in the evening (to be confirmed).
vd:aranda: A historic churrería in the centre: churros and porras to dip in thick hot chocolate. Eaten standing or at little tables, with a queue especially on Saturday and Sunday mornings.
vp:aranda: Churros with chocolate about €4–6 (Cargest and guides, menu not seen). Hours vary by half an hour between sources (InYourPocket gives 7:30am–1pm and 5–9pm): to be confirmed.
vd:canasta: A bakery-pâtisserie on the main square, with fresh bread, pastries and sandwiches. For a quick breakfast (coffee and tostada) or a snack to take away.
vp:canasta: Breakfast about €2–5 (Cargest, menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:julieta: A bright café-pâtisserie near Calle Larios: coffee, cakes, pastries and bigger breakfasts, with some choice for anyone wanting something other than the usual tostada.
vp:julieta: Breakfast about €6–12 per person (Cargest, menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:quitapenas: A bodega with barrels of sweet Málaga wine, vermouth and simple tapas: fried boquerones, anchovies, cured meats and cheeses. Open every day, a short walk from Calle Larios.
vp:quitapenas: Tapas from about €3–6, wine by the glass €2–4 (menu not seen). Hours from andalucia.org, to be confirmed.
vd:lola: An always-packed tavern on a street in the centre, with croquetas, grilled prawns, ajoblanco malagueño and small montaditos, to have with a cold vermouth. Best to arrive early or book.
vp:lola: Tapas from €3.50 to €6 (Malaga Travel Guide, menu not seen); a light meal about €15–22 per person. Hours from TableJourney, to be confirmed.
vd:pimpi: The city's most famous bodega, in a palace with many rooms and barrels signed by celebrities. Taste sweet Málaga wine with tapas like berenjenas con miel (aubergine with honey), opposite the Roman Theatre and the Alcazaba. Popular with tourists, but still a classic.
vp:pimpi: Tapas €4–7, sweet wine about €3 (Malaga Travel Guide, menu not seen). Hours from andalucia.org, to be confirmed: it generally stays open until 2am, on Fridays and Saturdays until 3am.
vd:guardia: Málaga's oldest bodega, opened in 1840: wooden barrels along the bar and the bill chalked up by the barman. Drink sweet or dry Málaga wine and order seafood and tapas at the counter.
vp:guardia: A glass of wine costs a few euros, tapas and seafood about €4–10 (menu not seen). Hours from InYourPocket, to be confirmed: closed on Sundays.
vd:atarazanas_bar: The bar inside the market: fried fish, boquerones with lemon and prawn skewers, served standing at a metal counter. Very crowded at lunchtime.
vp:atarazanas_bar: Tapas and fish portions about €5–10 (Malaga Travel Guide, menu not seen). Hours and Sunday closing from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:casapicasso: The house where Picasso was born, on Plaza de la Merced.
cd:botanico: A subtropical garden with ponds and waterfalls, north of the city.
cx:botanico: It's about 6 km from the centre.
cd:museovetro: Glass from all over Europe in an 18th-century house.
cd:catamaran: An hour at sea from the Muelle Uno, with the city behind you.
cd:museoruso: Russian art from the 15th century, in the former tobacco factory.
